defect.summary: Budget-scale figures used compact currency notation, which cannot resolve the product's own $5,000 granularity.
defect.detail: compactCurrency (src/app.js:17-22) uses notation:'compact' with maximumFractionDigits:0. Allocations move in $5,000 steps and the solver searches a $25,000 grid, but compact rounds to $100,000 steps at the millions scale. $1,200,000 and $1,195,000 both rendered '$1M'. The page could not show the difference between a fully committed budget and one $5,000 short.
defect.notAFractionDigitsSetting: Every compact configuration collides: maximumFractionDigits 0, 1 and 2 and maximumSignificantDigits:3 all render $1,200,000 and $1,195,000 identically. Asserted in tests/model.test.js so the assumption fails loudly if Intl behaviour ever changes.

repair.summary: Use the existing exact formatMoney (src/app.js:50) for every budget-scale figure; keep compact for dense cells.

beyondLiteralScope.reasoning: These restate budget-scale or user-specified figures. Leaving them compact would print '$1,200,000' in the headline and '$1M committed' in the activity trail on the same screen, and the demo's key beat would echo a $1,195,000 request back as '$1M'.
beyondLiteralScope.revert: git diff 51f2a13 -- src/app.js  (the four addActivity call sites)
